jurisdiction.name: Thailand
local_terms: หนูท้องขาว

summary: Thailand is permissive by default for the roof rat. The Wild Animal Conservation and Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019) regulates only species on its reserved/protected/controlled schedules — and R. rattus is on none of them; it's treated throughout Thai law as an unprotected agricultural pest (a major rice-field pest). So keeping/breeding/selling a captive-bred roof rat falls outside the wildlife-permit system, subject only to the Cruelty Prevention & Welfare of Animals Act B.E. 2557 (2014) care duties; fancy rats and small rodents are sold openly (e.g., Chatuchak market). Bangkok's 2026 pet ordinance adds animal-density rules but doesn't single out small rodents. The one permit step is IMPORT: bringing a live rodent into Thailand needs a Department of Livestock Development (DLD) import permit + a 30-day quarantine + an origin health certificate (R. rattus isn't CITES-listed). Internal inter-province movement technically falls under the broad Animal Epidemics Act paperwork chain, but that targets livestock and isn't enforced against private pet rodents. No Thai law expressly prohibits private keeping/breeding/transfer of captive-bred R. rattus.

keep.why: R. rattus is not on any DNP reserved/protected/controlled wildlife schedule under WACPA B.E. 2562 (which regulates only scheduled species); it's formally treated as agricultural vermin. The welfare act (B.E. 2557) imposes care duties on any kept animal but restricts no non-listed species. Bangkok's 2026 ordinance density rules target goat/pig-scale animals, not rat cages. Pest status + absence from any protected list + open pet-rodent retail strongly imply unregulated keeping; 'unclear' only because no official text affirmatively exempts R. rattus.
keep.governing_law: Wild Animal Conservation & Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019) (scheduled species only); Cruelty Prevention & Welfare of Animals Act B.E. 2557 (2014).

breed.why: Breeding a non-scheduled, non-CITES species is outside the WACPA permit system (which targets scheduled species). No DLD licence specifically for rodent breeding was found (DLD breeding licensing covers livestock/aquaculture). Chatuchak openly sells small rodents without a species-specific breeding licence. At commercial 'pet shop'/'animal farm' scale, Bangkok's 2026 ordinance health-hazardous-business clause could require a BMA district health-business permit.
breed.governing_law: WACPA B.E. 2562 s.9 (controlled-wildlife breeding permit — N/A to unlisted); Bangkok 2026 ordinance (commercial premises).

sell_give.why: Sale/gifting of a non-scheduled species isn't regulated under WACPA (trade restrictions apply only to scheduled/controlled wildlife). No statute bars selling/transferring captive-bred R. rattus between private parties. A commercial pet business needs general DBD business registration + possibly a BMA health-business licence for premises (business-operation, not species-specific). Free/non-commercial transfer appears unregulated beyond welfare duties. Not CITES-listed.
sell_give.governing_law: WACPA B.E. 2562 (scheduled species only); DBD/BMA business registration (premises).

transport.why: IMPORT needs a DLD import permit before travel (Form R1/1; ≥7 days ahead) + a mandatory 30-day quarantine at a government Animal Quarantine Station + an origin-government vet health certificate; DLD states 'other species (birds, reptiles, rodents) require additional permission.' Not CITES-listed. INTERNAL inter-province movement technically falls under the Animal Epidemics Act B.E. 2558 R-form chain, but that targets agricultural livestock and isn't enforced against private pet rats (a negligible-enforcement gray zone). Never release.
transport.governing_law: DLD import permit (Form R1/1) + quarantine; Animal Epidemics Act B.E. 2558 (internal, broad).

restrictions.summary: Keeping/breeding/selling a captive-bred roof rat in Thailand needs no wildlife permit (R. rattus is unscheduled), only welfare-law care. The one permit step is IMPORT: a DLD import permit (apply ≥7 days ahead) + a 30-day quarantine + an origin health certificate. Commercial premises may need a BMA business/health licence. Never release.
steps: For import: apply for a DLD import permit (Form R1/1) + arrange 30-day quarantine + obtain origin health certificate
restrictions.where_to_file: Department of Livestock Development (DLD) — Animal Quarantine & Inspection

inquiry_focus: (1) Is Rattus rattus (หนูดำ/หนูท้องขาว) listed as reserved, protected, or controlled wildlife under any ministerial notification under the Wild Animal Conservation & Protection Act B.E. 2562? If not listed, does any provision apply to a private hobbyist keeping/captive-breeding it? (2) (DLD) What are the full health/documentation requirements for importing captive-bred R. rattus as pets, and does the Animal Epidemics Act B.E. 2558 require an R1/2 movement document for domestic inter-province transport of captive-bred pet rodents? (3) (DLD) Is there any DLD registration/licence for a hobbyist who breeds R. rattus at home and gives offspring to vetted individuals at no charge in Bangkok?
